analysis.title: GS Materials Nov 3...Coppers show me. story, Indonesian blueprint...
key_insights: James McGeoch asks how China solves the shortage of onshore copper stocks, pointing to fabricator utilisation, copper rod operating rates, power industry processing fees and scrap utilisation as the data to watch. He says he does not see how China solves the lack of stockpiles.
China-linked equities traded fine on the day: metals, steels, air conditioners, construction and property. Coals were the one weaker group, with CKCA down 2.5%.
AAL.LN extended the MMG nickel long stop date to Dec 31. The desk says this is not stock moving.
KAP.LI posted Q3 (uranium market update) with production improved across all assets and guidance unchanged.

ERO.CN reported an earnings beat, held production guidance and raised its C1 cost guide by 10c/lb on FX, ME and grades. The desk says it has been an uneventful period for the copper producers, who absorbed weather issues through realised prices and by-products.

Nickel rallied 1% after Indonesia's minister Bahlil urged restrained output and said mining work plans should be used to control nickel supply and demand. He said 'If prices are currently not high or favorable, then leave it in the ground'.

GS raised its TTF gas forecast for 1Q27 to EUR74 (from EUR44) and its 2027 average to EUR51 (from EUR32). The change reflects a subjective 45% probability of a low-winter, Mideast LNG supply scenario (worth EUR26 on 1Q27 prices) and a small cold-weather risk component (worth EUR4).

Copper weakness is tied to CNH, KOSPI and AI. The desk understands the CNH move on the back of the RRR hike and says the arbitrage remains stable. It notes HGA underperformance as a view of where more risk is held.

The desk says the AI trade will end badly when physical assets collide with financial assets. Investor feedback centres on two questions: China wants the metal to keep electrifying and building AI platforms (yes), and the US wants to give the metal back to China (no).
GS's Global Investment Research (GIR) midterm preview expects a more aggressive tariff regime and a data centre acceleration. The desk continues to like the GSXGCOPP index.
Aramco Q3 net income was $31.2bn, 1.8% above consensus. Realised price fell to $95.20/bbl from $108 in Q2, and refining margins were very strong with record downstream, up 65% q/q.

Aramco said the Middle East conflict has caused a net loss of 1.8bn barrels, offset by SPR releases, the pipeline and non-Strait corridors. A reopening would take up to 18 months at 2.1mmbd to replenish inventories, with commercial inventories and SPRs largely exhausted.

The desk says mining equities are back to 2015 levels despite a strong copper price, with GLEN at 65p and AAL at 2 pounds in 2015. It calls this one big AI unwind and sees opportunity when sentiment recovers.

GLD had its first monthly outflow since June, -$1.8bn, nearly reversing September's inflows. The ETF did not see liquidation on the big move lower at the end of last week, and the desk says CTAs like trend and are not scared of leverage.

China equities had a volatile midday session on shrinking volumes. Policy support from the previous day failed to lift indices because measures were in line with expectations. Hard tech was hit hardest in the global tech selloff, CPO selling persisted, and defensives (agriculture, consumer, renewables) and non-bank financials rallied. Chatter about regulators slowing IPOs helped the close.
